title: POC Weekly — Velocity tuning & rollout plan
next_steps: Ethan to run 10k synthetic TTFT + streaming microburst tests (kernel: stream-opt) and share raw logs by 2026-07-12
LedgerWave to provide representative seqlen distribution and a 48-hour production sample by 2026-07-10
Samira to send updated pricing sheet with burst credits and dedicated vs hosted comparison by 2026-07-08
Schedule on-site latency demo (if pilot metrics look good) week of 2026-07-20
action_items: Ethan: run microburst + streaming TTFT sweep, attach KV cache on/off traces (due 2026-07-12)
Daniel: upload 48h traffic sample and seqlen histogram to shared drive (due 2026-07-10)
Samira: update pilot SOW with burst policy and cost delta (due 2026-07-08)
Rosa: validate onboarding checklist for VPC peering and cert install (due 2026-07-09)
header: Date: 2026-07-05 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 58m\nAttendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Daniel Kim (LedgerWave Eng Lead), Rosa Alvarez (LedgerWave SRE), Benji Ortiz (LedgerWave CTO), Maya Singh (LedgerWave Platform)
summary: Weekly POC sync covering recent TTFT numbers, streaming path microbursts, kernel choices, and a proposed pilot rollout that blends hosted burst credits with a short dedicated window. Main ask: LedgerWave to upload production sample; Redwood to run a larger synthetic sweep focusing on first-token and streaming microburst variance. Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: Kernel selection (stream-opt vs generic) and hedging
Pilot rollout: burst credits vs short reserved capacity
transcript:
00:00:00 - Samira: okay hey everyone, thanks for joining. um we're on for 58 minutes, i'll kick off. quick rollcall?
00:00:07 - Daniel: hey daniel here.
00:00:09 - Rosa: rosa on my side.
00:00:10 - Benji: benji here.
00:00:12 - Maya: maya present.
00:00:13 - Ethan: ethan from redwood.
00:00:14 - Priya: priya here.
00:00:16 - Samira: perfect cool. agenda — review last week's ttft numbers, go over streaming microburst logs ethan prepared, pick kernel strategy, agree on next steps for the pilot rollout.
00:00:30 - Daniel: sounds good.
00:00:32 - Ethan: quick context, last week we ran the small 1k baseline against your sample and noticed a long tail at the first token, and the stream-opt kernel was better on median but showed variance under microbursts. so we expanded to more runs.
00:00:49 - Rosa: yeah we saw that in our side too, when traffic spikes we get these 200–300 ms blips that push 95th to like 600, which is painful for the frontend.
00:01:02 - Benji: those blips — are they queuing on the ingress or at the kv-cash, sorry k v cash stage?
00:01:08 - Ethan: good question. the traces show most of the delta before dispatch, small chunk in kv cache miss path — sometimes transcription wrote it as K V cash — but basically cache miss plus kernel context switch.
00:01:25 - Daniel: can you repeat the numbers? median, p95 for both kernels?
00:01:29 - Ethan: sure. median first-token: generic kernel ~120ms, stream-opt ~98ms. p95 generic ~400ms, stream-opt ~560ms in our 5k runs. so stream-opt improves median but increases variance under concurrent microbursts in our harness.
00:01:50 - Priya: do we think that's because stream-opt does more work eagerly and blocks other streams?
00:01:56 - Ethan: that's the hypothesis — stream-opt aggressively fuses attention ops for streaming, which is great when isolated, but under bursty multiplexing it can cause kernel hogs.
00:02:07 - Samira: ok so tradeoff is median vs tail. ledgerwave's SLO was 200ms for first token for 95% of requests, right daniel?
00:02:15 - Daniel: right, 200ms p95 for interactive workloads. embeddings path is different but this is user-facing chat.
00:02:22 - Samira: so stream-opt alone doesn't meet that p95 in the current config. options: tune hedging, do a hybrid route, use dedicated short window for bursts, or tune batch size and kv caching.
00:02:36 - Maya: quick Q — how much does kv cache help p95? our cache hit rate is about 70% currently.
00:02:42 - Ethan: when hits are up, p95 drops a lot — in synthetic we saw p95 go from 560 to ~320 with cache hit bump to 95%. so improving hit rate is a big lever.
00:02:56 - Rosa: we can try warming and small TTLs but worried about memory with your kv design.
00:03:03 - Ethan: noted. also, sequence length distribution matters — you provided median seqlen 64 but 20% of traffic is 256+ which changes kernel behavior.
00:03:15 - Daniel: oh yeah that 20% is from some longform generative flows, we could maybe split routes.
00:03:21 - Benji: splitting routes might be simplest: short interactive route uses stream-opt with hedging, long-form uses generic kernel tuned for throughput.
00:03:31 - Samira: agreed, route by seqlen and intent. but we need to test hedging config — what did hedging look like in your runs?
00:03:39 - Ethan: we tried a soft hedge — if latency > 120ms spawn fallback on generic kernel after 60ms; it lowered p95 to ~300ms but increased token cost ~6%. hard hedge lowered p95 more but cost jumped 12%.
00:03:57 - Rosa: cost is acceptable if we reserve burst credits for those windows. are burst credits part of the pilot pricing?
00:04:03 - Samira: yes i'll add burst credits to the SOW, and show net delta hosted vs short reserved. i'll share a pricing scenario sheet.
00:04:11 - Daniel: timeline question — when can we expect a run at 10k+ with the actual seqlen mix? our real traffic has a heavier tail during biz hours.
00:04:19 - Ethan: we can schedule the bigger sweep this week but need the 48-hour sample from you to make the distribution realistic — otherwise we bias the run.
00:04:28 - Daniel: i'll upload that by monday.
00:04:31 - Priya: noted in action items.
00:04:34 - Samira: ok moving on — streaming microburst traces. ethan, walk us through a couple of examples.
00:04:40 - Ethan: slide-ish: (ref) link: https://redwood.internal/poc/ledgerwave-benchmarks — example A: traffic spike 1k qps for 5s, stream-opt node shows 2 blocked kernels concurrently for 80ms causing a small convoy. example B: mixed load with high seqlen tasks queued and small messages interleaving: scheduling preemption delayed streaming work by 110ms.
00:05:06 - Rosa: hmm that convoy pattern — is it a GPU scheduler issue or our request shaping?
00:05:12 - Ethan: looks like scheduling + our continuous batching. when batch windows align weirdly you get big fused kernels that take longer. we can reduce batch window to lower median but that increases per-token compute overhead.
00:05:26 - Benji: so again cost vs latency tradeoff.
00:05:29 - Samira: is there a quick config that gives better p95 without huge cost?
00:05:33 - Ethan: short term: enable hedging with conservative thresholds and reduce batch window slightly for streaming routes; medium term: kernel scheduler improvements we can prototype — but that's a 3–4 week engineering cycle.
00:05:46 - Daniel: for the pilot we need practical steps now, not multi-week dev.
00:05:49 - Ethan: agreed. so 3 practical items: 1) hedging soft fallback, 2) route splitting by seqlen, 3) improve kv cache hit rate by pre-warming for top N prefixes.
00:06:02 - Rosa: pre-warming — we'll need a safe list of prefixes, is there a tool to push warms?
00:06:07 - Ethan: we have a small warm API we can expose for the pilot; i'll include instructions.
00:06:12 - Maya: security question — will pre-warming touch any PII?
00:06:15 - Ethan: it will only store token-level KV for model inference, we never persist logs to S3 in the warm flow unless you opt in — will document encryption & KMS details.
00:06:25 - Samira: on the security front, ledgerwave asked about SOC 2 and audit logs last week — where are we on that?
00:06:30 - Priya: we shared SOC 2 attestation and the audit logs artifact (link provided). samira will follow up on any outstanding items.
00:06:38 - Daniel: good. any blockers for network peering?
00:06:41 - Rosa: just cert install and route policy; i have a checklist we'll post.
00:06:46 - Samira: great. back to numbers — daniel can you confirm the SLO again? is 200ms p95 for interactive the hard cut?
00:06:53 - Daniel: yes 200ms p95. if we can't get there we risk not enabling real-time chat in next sprint.
00:07:00 - Ethan: ok then i recommend: route split, soft hedging with careful thresholds, and pre-warm the top 20 prefixes — that should get us under 250ms p95 in most windows, maybe hitting 200ms once we bump cache to 90%+.
00:07:14 - Benji: acceptable as long as we track regressions and have rollback.
00:07:18 - Samira: we'll give rollback policies in the SOW; also canaries.
00:07:22 - Daniel: one more ask — can you run a night-run that simulates our diurnal spike pattern?
00:07:27 - Ethan: yes, provide the 48h sample and we'll replay it in the cluster and attach perf counters.
00:07:32 - Priya: adding that as an action.
00:07:35 - Samira: ok shifting to pilot rollout: we proposed a 2-week hosted pilot with burst credits, then a 2-week short reserved window for peak hours to validate SLOs. thoughts?
00:07:46 - Rosa: we prefer a dedicated window for burst hours to be safe — if the hosted pilot can't hit p95 we need fallback.
00:07:53 - Benji: agree on a hybrid — hosted + scheduled reserved capacity during peak. keeps cost reasonable.
00:07:58 - Daniel: timeline — can we do the hosted pilot next week?
00:08:01 - Samira: yes, if we get the sample and SOW signed early next week we can start.
00:08:06 - Maya: what about region placement? we need EU residency for some clients — any implications?
00:08:11 - Ethan: we can pin model variants and route to eu-west region; there is slight latency delta but shouldn't affect these p95 goals if clients are EU.
00:08:19 - Daniel: okay we'll flag which routes need EU.
00:08:22 - Samira: quick note on metrics — we'll instrument per-route ttft, p50/p95/p99, token cost, and kv hit rate. you'll get dashboards in console.
00:08:31 - Priya: dashboard access will be provisioned by me after SOW.
00:08:34 - Samira: any outstanding open questions from ledgerwave?
00:08:37 - Rosa: certs and network checklist — we'll share it today.
00:08:40 - Benji: are you comfortable with the rollback plan?
00:08:42 - Ethan: yes, two-tier rollback: route-level fallback to generic kernel + drop hedging, and infra-level reserved capacity off-ramp.
00:08:51 - Daniel: ok good.
00:08:53 - Samira: final recap: daniel uploads 48h sample by 2026-07-10, ethan runs 10k synthetic sweep with hedging + stream-opt and shares logs by 2026-07-12, samira sends updated SOW and pricing 2026-07-08, rosa validates cert/install checklist 2026-07-09. we schedule a follow-up on 2026-07-13 to review results.
00:09:12 - Daniel: sounds good.
00:09:14 - Benji: quick comment — competitor callouts: we've been poking at DeepServe internally; curious on your integration differences.
00:09:22 - Samira: quick aside: DeepServe has a simpler streaming implementation but less kernel fusion and fewer hedging controls; CloudLM did okay on throughput but was worse on tail. we'll share a short comparison note.
00:09:34 - Ethan: i'll add technical notes to the repo.
00:09:37 - Priya: ok i'll schedule the 7/13 follow-up, invite same attendees.
00:09:41 - Samira: thanks everyone. end of call.

Note: transcription contains occasional label errors and minor word swaps (e.g., "kv-cash" instead of "KV cache").
